request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Hardware Wallet Maintenance 2026 covering 12 months of production maintenance for Cardano hardware-wallet support.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,310,960 ada, split into 1,272,777 ada for Cardano Hardware Wallet Maintenance & Compatibility Assurance and 38,183 ada for the Intersect Budget Administration fee.
The work is described as a continuity proposal for an already-proven Cardano hardware-wallet access layer rather than a new wallet product.

The proposer claims continuous maintenance is needed because Cardano protocol evolution, Ledger and Trezor release cycles, and wallet and dApp integration demand create compatibility risk for a security-critical access layer.

The stated scope is limited to compatibility, security, supporting libraries and tooling, release support, vendor-required audit work, and developer support, and is said not to duplicate broader core-node, ledger, or general infrastructure maintenance budgets.

The proposer claims the proposal aligns primarily with Pillar 1 by preserving secure, reliable, interoperable signing, and secondarily with Pillar 2 by supporting secure UX, developer experience, and compatibility for adoption.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced on-chain under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The proposer states the requested amount did not, at submission, breach the 350M ada Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713, either alone or in aggregate.

The proposal states that funds will be administered through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts, with a 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract, one Project-Specific Smart Contract, specified addresses, role-based approvals, and an Oversight Committee of six external entities.
The proposal says a dashboard at treasury.sundae.fi and on-chain records will allow the community to audit the TRSC or PSSC and track metrics related to the withdrawn ada.
The document discloses prior treasury and Catalyst funding links related to hardware wallet maintenance, Ledger app work, Plutus enhancement, and several security or developer ecosystem projects.

summary: The anchor describes a 1,310,960 ada treasury withdrawal submitted by Intersect for 2026 hardware-wallet maintenance, with a single work package, an administration fee, NCL and Hydra voting assertions, prior-funding disclosures, and smart-contract-based treasury administration details, but it does not provide a complete budget analysis, feasibility analysis, risk analysis, alternatives analysis, or failure-mode analysis in the supplied text.
